interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Distance Scott travels to school" e "Distance Greg travels to school"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Yes; Scott is right. He does live farther away."; "No; Scott is wrong. It is Greg who lives father away."; "Both live the same distance from the school."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

Scott's fraction is 13/..., so count the parts named by the bottom number.

How can you locate thirteen tenths when each interval represents one tenth?
Start at zero and count equal tenth intervals until you reach thirteen tenths.
Ten tenths reach one whole mile, so the target is three tenths beyond one.
Place the marker at the third tenth interval after 1 and submit the fraction represented by that point.
What does the bottom number in Greg's fraction tell you about each whole?
Read Greg's denominator and enter it in the denom2 field before confirming.
Greg's fraction is 5/3, so the unit interval must be divided into thirds.
Enter the denominator below Greg's fraction bar and confirm three equal intervals.
How can you locate five thirds when each interval represents one third?
Start at zero and count five equal third intervals along Greg's line.
Three thirds make one whole mile, so the target is two thirds beyond one.

Which marked point is farther to the right on the two number lines?

exercicio.statement:
Scott and Greg both are students at the Carmite Middle School. Scott thinks he is always late to school because he lives too far away. One day, they compared the distances they must travel to figure out who lives farther.
Scott travels 13/10 miles to get to school.
Greg travels 5/3 miles to get to school.
Who lives farther from the school?
